newsitem.title: CANADA: Norcen to make bid for Basic.
newsitem.headline: Norcen to make bid for Basic.

text.p: Norcen Energy Resources Ltd and Basic Petroleum International Ltd said on Tuesday they reached a deal under which Norcen will offer US$40 per share for up to 97.5 percent of Basic or a total of US$303 million.
Norcen's offer will be for up to 7,572,064 shares of Basic's common stock.
The offer, due to begin on May 12, is conditional on Norcen receiving more than 50 percent of Basic's shares on a fully diluted basis, and on other customary conditions.

The companies said the bid will be followed by a merger in which those shareholders who do not tender will get either cash or a combination of cash and a royalty right relating to certain exploration lands.
Norcen has reached an agreement with Basic shareholders representing over 47 percent of the outstanding shares and has received their approval and support of the transaction.
"This acquisition is an excellent fit with Norcen's operating approach," Norcen President and Chief Executive Grant Billing said in a statement.
"It adds substantial incremental cash flow and it is a focused operation with high working interest combined with production growth potential and exploration upside," he added.

Basic Petroleum's operations are in Guatemala and the company has current production of roughly 23,000 barrels per day. Proven reserves are estimated at 65 million barrels with 18 million barrels of probable reserves. There are four fields already in production with more than 1.5 million acres of exploratory acreage available.

Norcen will be purchasing the company for a total of US$303 million in cash plus a royalty right relating to certain exploration lands. After the deal is complete, Norcen's debt-to-cash flow ratio will be approximately 1.5 times. The companies said Norcen will fully integrate Basic Petroleum's operations into its own prior to year-end.
